title: Interior-zero complexity of polynomial differentiation residuals
abstract: We classify the numbers of interior zeros that permit vanishing and superalgebraic differentiation residuals for polynomials whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. If a degree-$n$ polynomial has exactly $M$ strictly interior zeros, then, for every complex slope, its normalized $H^2$ residual is at least $n/[2\sqrt216^M(n+2M+4)^{2M+2}]$. Consequently a prescribed budget $b_n$ permits a superalgebraically small residual sequence if and only if $b_n\to\infty$. Sufficiency holds with real coefficients, normalization at the origin, the slope fixed by that normalization, and exactly $b_n$ interior zeros. In contrast, one interior zero already permits residuals $O(n^{-1/6})$, with family-specific asymptotic constant $\sqrt{15}/4^{4/3}$, whereas the circle-only infimum tends to $1/\sqrt8$. For one interior zero we also prove a universal $c n^{-13/6}$ lower bound; the optimal rate remains open. The finite-budget obstruction combines a reciprocal identity with classical Mahler, truncated-shift and Poisson-kernel estimates, and extends to a stable factor times a self-inversive cofactor. For unrestricted interior counts we prove $\exp(-C\sqrt n)$ lower bounds for every $C>\sqrt{(8/3)\log17}$. The upper construction corrects both the exact slope and degree rounding at every large degree. The resulting refinement of exterior power-sum bounds uses a known residual method; the negative answer to Erdos Problem 973 was already known. No matching fixed-budget rates or stretched-exponential upper bounds are claimed.
